questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam cultural melting pot with a highly international profile and UvA has a strong media department. Another reason I chose this city was due to its unique aesthetical beauty and atmosphere, which I fell in love with years ago when I first came to visit.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This has been my heaven in every way possible. Academically, creatively and socially.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Uva provided the necessary information and introduction meetings, and it always seemed clear who to contact if I had any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My living quarters was solely set up online through Lieven de Key but I didn't experience any problems. I attended the introduction meeting for exchange students at the humanities department which was sufficient. Assistance could always be given through contacting the international office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky through the lottery. I know Amsterdam has a housing challenge, and not everyone is so lucky. My best recommendation is to start early in multiple facebook groups and through network, and probably accept the possibility of living pretty far away from the center. It's definitely a "risk" that should be taken into account.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I rented a bike through Swapfiets, but many of my peers bought a used one in the city. Public transportation is expensive so I think one should be ready to bike a lot when choosing Amsterdam.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was lucky, but it probably would have been difficult otherwise. However, most people I know did manage to find something in the end. Start looking as early as possible has to be the main advice.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process is a bit back and forth, but if you are ready to make some compromise (if some courses are filled up or cancelled) it's not too difficult. Also, don't hesitate to reach out to the international office via mail, they will help.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I never experienced a problem or question that could not be solved when reaching out to the international office via mail. This is my best advice. Don't hesitate to write a mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got one of my top priorities and then ended up with three courses that wasn't my original choices. But in the end I liked them, and in that sense I consider it quite successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be too religious about your priorities. Be open minded - it's unlikely that you will get every course you hope for, but you never know if the alternative might turn out even better.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a good balance between theory and practice. Some teacher were better than others I believe is fair to say, but overall a high level and challenging in a stimulating way. Also I experienced a lot of freedom in the exam projects and I appreciate that.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is high and you will have rich opportunity to participate and be challenged. The grading is quite tough.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UvA I experienced more creative freedom and in-class activities with students. It seems more focused on connecting theory to the practical world outside, which I believe is a quality.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Creativity, Innovation and Entrepreneurship in the Humanities
- AI and the New Conditions of Creativity
- Co-Creation and Critical Curating: The Futures of Culture and its Institutions
- Sustainable Digital Media? Automation, Technosolutionism and Care

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I recommend:
- Creativity, Innovation and Entrepreneurship in the Humanities
- AI and the New Conditions of Creativity
- Sustainable Digital Media? Automation, Technosolutionism and Care

These courses provide a good balance between theory and practices. The first one is very good if you like to work with business ideas and the second (AI) is especially creative and quite unique - this might also be due to the fact that the teacher of the course, Gabriel, is one of the best I ever experienced.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I cannot recall any significant unexpected costs. Maybe I was a bit surprised by how expensive public transport is in Amsterdam and the costs of food in general.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Buying groceries and going out for a beer was actually the same as in Copenhagen, which I did not anticipate.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's my favorite city in the world so you will not miss amusement. My only critique on clubs is: too much techno music to my taste, but this is a problem I encounter in almost every city.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can do sports and fitness at facilities connected to the university or erasmus programme, but I personally didn't so I cannot say much about it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Rijks museum, Stedelijk and Van Gogh because of its world class art. Go on a boat along the canals because it's charming and beautiful. Book a ticket to Skate Cafe because it's a unique night club that doesn't look like anything else.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit other parts of Netherlands, easily accessible by train. Take a trip to Belgium (Gent or Antwerp). You're close to so many historical cities and cites. Make use of it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Coming from Copenhagen it wasn't difficult, but of course the first couple of weeks are weird when you don't know anyone. Give yourself time. Be king to yourself and remember - you WILL adjust if you are willing to meet new people. It just takes a little bit of time. But in Amsterdam there is room for everyone, from every culture. That's part of the beauty.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I am quite a social person so it wasn't hard although I travelled alone. But check out all the Erasmus events. People are very nice and welcoming. The Erasmus Student Network will take care of you if you feel lonely. Reach out to them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural difference challenging personally. But sometimes people only hang out in groups with their own people (from same countries) and I understand if someone would feel a bit excluded in this regard.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: As an old trade capital, you feel how cultures from all over the world come together. It's also an innovative culture with lots of creativity and surprises.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Start the housing search early.
2. Get a bike immediately.
3. Be prepared for independent study.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I recommend joining ISN Amsterdam events during the introduction week. It’s the easiest way to make friends outside of your specific courses. Also, make sure to keep a close eye on your OLA and digital signatures early on, as navigating the digital systems between UCPH and UvA can take some time.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Personal growth  from living independently in this vibrant, international city. I loved meeting students from all over the world, experiencing the unique cultural and social life of Amsterdam, and adapting to a new academic environment at a highly ranked university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a good balance between studying for exams and enjoying the exchange experience took some time to figure out.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
